Modern.tagline: Sleep medicine, organised around your chronotype.
Modern.brandNameRationale: Chronotype — the term sleep medicine uses for an individual's circadian preference (lark, owl, in-between) — is owned by no one and useful to everyone. Strongest of Agent A's modern row: Hypnos Health was flagged by Agent A for the Hypnos Beds collision, Circadia was flagged for skincare collisions. Chronotype is the modern-clinic word that the actual evidence base uses.
Modern.industrySummary: Modern sleep clinics in 2025+ compete with at-home wearable diagnostics (Oura, Eight Sleep) and big-box sleep labs. Patients are 30-55, often have tried melatonin and a sleep app, and want a clinical workup without the hospital-overnight feel. The opening is a clinic that owns the chronotype framework and runs in-home polysomnography.
Modern.competitorLandscape: Stanford Sleep Center (stanfordhealthcare.org) holds the academic tier. Tuck (tuck.com) is the consumer information peer. Eight Sleep (eightsleep.com) competes from the device side. We sit smaller, clinician-led, and chronotype-organised.
Modern.positioningStatement: A sleep clinic organised around chronotype, with in-home polysomnography.

targetAudience.primary: 32 to 55. Has worn an Oura ring for a year and has more questions than answers. Wants a sleep physician, a real study, and a written plan. Pays out of pocket if insurance is slow.
behaviors: Reads the physician's CV before booking
Brings their wearable data to the consult

dos: Name the sleep physician and their boards

Modern.logoDirection: A wordmark — CHRONOTYPE CLINIC set in a precise modern serif, with a small horizontal sine-wave glyph above the O suggesting the circadian curve. The sine wave alone works as the favicon and on the appointment card.

typography.primary: GT Sectra for the wordmark and patient letters
typography.secondary: Söhne for the booking flow and body
typography.rationale: Sectra carries the clinical-heritage weight; Söhne keeps the booking flow modern.

Luxury.tagline: A private sleep practice in the Kleitman tradition.
Luxury.brandNameRationale: Nathaniel Kleitman (1895-1999) co-discovered REM sleep in 1953 at the University of Chicago — the founding fact of sleep medicine — and lived to 104. Strongest of Agent A's heritage row for luxury: Kleitman & Dement is fine but two-name partnership reads less elite, Dement Hall is correct but Dement died only in 2020 making the name feel more recent. The Kleitman Practice inherits 70 years of unimpeachable lineage and lands as a discreet private clinic.
Luxury.industrySummary: Luxury sleep medicine serves the patient who treats their sleep physician like a private banker — the same clinician for every visit, no waiting room, a full overnight at home with their own staff. The opening is a practice that revives the consulting-physician posture for sleep.
Luxury.competitorLandscape: Lanserhof (lanserhof.com) holds the European medical-spa tier with a sleep arm. The Cleveland Clinic Sleep Center (my.clevelandclinic.org) is the academic peer. SleepScore Labs (sleepscore.com) sits on the device side. We sit as the urban private consulting practice.
Luxury.positioningStatement: A discreet private sleep practice in the consulting-physician tradition.

targetAudience.primary: 45 to 70. Has a private GP and a private dentist and wants a sleep physician in the same register. Travels often across time zones. Pays the invoice the same day.
behaviors: Books by phone, never by app
Expects the same physician for every visit

Luxury.logoDirection: A serif wordmark with elegant ligatures. A small embossed door-plate mark — a brass crescent — sits beneath the wordmark, used on the practice card, the sleep report, and the surgery door.

colorPalette.name: Practice Navy
colorPalette.meaning: The quiet of a private surgery at night.

typography.primary: Canela for the wordmark and printed material
typography.rationale: A high-contrast classical serif carries the consulting register; the grotesk handles the one digital surface.

Minimal.tagline: A sleep clinic for the people who can't.
Minimal.brandNameRationale: Long Night names the insomniac's experience without dramatising it — and 'long' is also a clinical descriptor of sleep latency. Strongest of Agent A's evocative row for minimal: The REM Hour is warm but technical, Sleep Debt House risks reading scolding. Long Night is two plain words that the patient already says to themselves at 3am.
Minimal.industrySummary: Minimal sleep clinics serve patients who want one thing — to sleep — without the hospital workup or the consumer-tech bundle. The opening is a clinic that publishes its prices, its physician, and the wait time, and stops there.
Minimal.competitorLandscape: Tuck (tuck.com) holds the minimal information peer. Big Health (bighealth.com) is the CBT-i app peer. Local independent sleep physicians compete on relationship. We publish less than any of them.
Minimal.positioningStatement: A sleep clinic. Published prices. One physician. CBT-i and a study.

targetAudience.primary: Adults 30-55 who've had insomnia for more than three months. They've tried melatonin, an app, and the GP. They want a sleep physician, a written plan, and the appointment to start on time.
behaviors: Books an initial and a follow-up
Reads the price list before booking

dos: Publish the price list on the home page

Minimal.logoDirection: A wordmark only. LONG NIGHT in a single-weight grotesk, wide kerned, all caps. No icon. The wordmark works on the door, the report cover, and the appointment card.

typography.rationale: One face. The sign, the card, and the site all carry the same wordmark.

Corporate.tagline: A multi-site sleep medicine partnership in the Stanford tradition.
Corporate.brandNameRationale: William C. Dement (1928-2020), the founder of the Stanford Sleep Research Center in 1970 and the man who effectively created the field of clinical sleep medicine. Strongest of Agent A's heritage row for corporate: Kleitman & Dement was used for the luxury slot, Stanford Lane Sleep risks the Stanford TM. Dement alone is safe (he died 2020, public-figure name), carries the institutional weight, and lands as a serious DSO-style sleep group.
Corporate.industrySummary: Corporate sleep medicine in 2025+ is consolidating around at-home diagnostics and CPAP-adherence programs. The next tier competes on physician retention and outcomes. The opening is a partnership-model group positioned on Stanford-lineage seriousness rather than franchise mechanics.
Corporate.competitorLandscape: Sleep Number (sleepnumber.com) is the consumer adjacency. ResMed (resmed.com) holds the device-and-services peer. Stanford Sleep (stanfordhealthcare.org) is the academic peer. We sit clinician-led, multi-site, and Stanford-traditioned.
Corporate.positioningStatement: A clinician-led sleep medicine partnership in the Stanford tradition.

targetAudience.primary: Procurement officers at insurers, HR directors at large employers, and sleep physicians considering joining a group. They sign multi-year contracts and care about physician retention, CPAP adherence rates, and OSA-claim reduction.
behaviors: Reviews clinical KPIs and adherence data
Values physician retention as a buying signal

dos: Lead with physician retention and adherence
Speak the language of insurance and procurement

Corporate.logoDirection: A wordmark with a small geometric mark — a single horizontal sine wave (the hypnogram) — to the left. Reads cleanly on uniforms, signage, and procurement decks.

typography.secondary: Source Serif Pro for printed clinical letters
typography.rationale: Inter scales cleanly across procurement decks; the serif handles the printed clinical letters.

Creative.tagline: A sleep clinic organised around the architecture of the night.
Creative.brandNameRationale: Sleep spindles are the bursts of brain activity that mark Stage 2 sleep, and 'stages' are how sleep medicine maps the night (N1, N2, N3, REM). Strongest of Agent A's craft row for creative: The Polysomnogram Clinic is honest but reads hospital-PR, EEG & Pillow is fine but the EEG image is overused. Spindle & Stage names the actual architecture and reads like a craft studio rather than a sleep lab.
Creative.industrySummary: Creative sleep clinics sit in the register of a designed bedroom shop or a craft science museum. Patients are design-literate, often in adjacent fields, and want a clinic that takes the architecture of sleep seriously and presents it beautifully. The opening is a brand with print-shop, illustrated, hypnogram-rich identity.
Creative.competitorLandscape: Casper (casper.com) holds the design-led adjacency. Eight Sleep (eightsleep.com) competes on device aesthetics. SleepScore Labs (sleepscore.com) sits on the data-pretty side. We sit as the clinic with print and illustration, not the brand with a clinic on the side.
Creative.positioningStatement: A sleep clinic organised around the architecture of the night.

targetAudience.primary: 30 to 48. Editors, designers, architects. Has read Walker's Why We Sleep and finished it. Will pay for a clinic that presents the hypnogram as a craft object.
behaviors: Buys the illustrated stage chart for the bedroom
Photographs the report — once — and never again

dos: Commission a yearly illustrated hypnogram chart
Print the report on heavy paper
Name each consult room after a sleep stage
donts: Use stock photos of people in bed

Creative.logoDirection: A wordmark in a chunky display serif with letterpress impression. The ampersand is set as a small woodblock-style sleep-spindle waveform. A standalone spindle mark for stickers and the report cover.

colorPalette.name: Night Indigo
colorPalette.meaning: The colour of the hypnogram at REM.

typography.primary: GT Sectra Display for the wordmark and illustrated charts
typography.secondary: GT Sectra Book for the printed reports
typography.rationale: One family, two cuts. The display reads woodblock; the book weight handles the printed reports.
